guard: cotal ps reports a partial census and exits non-zero instead of presenting one instance's seats as the whole space
why: The defect had two halves and each has its own mutation. Restoring the zero exit is the half a
script reads, so it is proven against the command's own status rather than against a helper.
Counting a refusing instance as one that reported restores the miscount the exit is derived
from. The last two hold the line the issue asked for: the split is decided on the structured
refusal code, and the code has to travel from the scatter to the renderer for the operator to
see it at all, which only the live run crosses.
No build step is needed: the suite imports the CLI from src, and nothing here mutates a package
The later six hold the #1637 review: invalid and superseded replies are rows the census counts,
a counted reply is not doubled by a stray, an empty refusal message stays a refusal, the notice
agrees in number, and the pinned pair prints input before output.

mutations.name: the partial census exits 0 again
mutations.expectRed: EXITS NON-ZERO: a partial census is not a listing of the space
mutations.cell: `cotal ps` over this space EXITS NON-ZERO: a partial census is not a listing of the space
mutations.note: This is the shipped behaviour and reproduces the half of #1637 that only a script can see.

mutations.name: a refusing instance is counted as one that reported
mutations.expectRed: the refusal and the silence counted the same way
mutations.cell: ...so two did not, the refusal and the silence counted the same way
mutations.note: The refusal hides that instance's whole roster, so counting it as reported is the miscount the exit status is derived from.

mutations.name: the notice is withheld from a partial census
mutations.expectRed: a partial census produces a notice
mutations.cell: a partial census produces a notice
mutations.note: An exit code with no line beside it tells an operator at a terminal nothing about what is missing.

mutations.name: the contract split is decided on the message instead of the code
mutations.expectRed: a refusal whose MESSAGE reads like a mismatch but carries no code is not one either
mutations.cell: ...and a refusal whose MESSAGE reads like a mismatch but carries no code is not one either
mutations.note: The wording is operator copy; a renderer matched to its prose claims a split for any refusal that mentions a contract.

mutations.name: the scatter stops carrying the refusal code to the renderer
mutations.expectRed: naming the contract split once, with the pin, off the code the scatter carried
mutations.cell: ...and naming the contract split once, with the pin, off the code the scatter carried
mutations.note: The census keys on the code, so dropping it in the scatter leaves the operator with the per-row SPEC citation and no statement of the condition.

mutations.name: an instance whose only answer was an invalid frame drops out of the projection again
mutations.find: instances.push({ instanceId, reachable: true, error: `answered with an invalid reply: ${message}`, code: "invalid-reply" });
mutations.expectRed: an instance whose only answer was an INVALID frame is a row that did not report its seats
mutations.cell: an instance whose only answer was an INVALID frame is a row that did not report its seats
mutations.note: The #1637 review's blocking case: core marks the scatter incomplete for an invalid frame, and the census can only count the rows it is handed.

mutations.name: a slot whose reply was voided by re-registration drops out of the projection again
mutations.replace: for (const { instanceId, reason } of [] as typeof result.churn) {
mutations.expectRed: an instance that re-registered mid-listing did not report either
mutations.cell: an instance that re-registered mid-listing did not report either
mutations.note: Registration churn drops a slot's counted reply, so the slot is uncovered; projecting only replies and missing lost it.

mutations.name: a stray epoch-churn reply beside a counted one adds a second row for the same instance
mutations.find:
for (const { instanceId, reason } of result.churn) {
    if (seen.has(instanceId)) continue;
mutations.expectRed: a stray reply from another epoch BESIDE a counted one leaves that instance reported, once
mutations.cell: ...but a stray reply from another epoch BESIDE a counted one leaves that instance reported, once
mutations.note: Core keeps a valid reply at the frozen epoch counted despite a stray from another incarnation; the projection must not turn that instance into a missing one.

mutations.name: a refusal with an empty message reads as an answer that reported
mutations.expectRed: a refusal with an EMPTY message is still a refusal, to the census and the renderer alike
mutations.cell: a refusal with an EMPTY message is still a refusal, to the census and the renderer alike
mutations.note: With ?? an empty message survives as the error: the census still counts it, but the renderer reads error by truthiness and prints the slot as an answer.

mutations.name: the partial-listing notice stops agreeing in number
mutations.expectRed: that names how many instances did not report, in the plural
mutations.cell: ...that names how many instances did not report, in the plural
mutations.note: Every review of the first head read the notice as ungrammatical for two or more instances.

mutations.name: the split line prints the pinned digest pair reversed
mutations.expectRed: and a second line naming the split, the pinned digests, and the instance they came from
mutations.cell: ...and a second line naming the split, the pinned digests, and the instance they came from
mutations.note: The first head's cell asserted each digest's presence, not their order, and a review's reversed-pair mutant survived it.
